question: A thief steals a bike at 12:30 p.m. and drives it at 48 km/h. But the theft is discovered after half an hour. The bike owner starts to chase him on another bike at 58 km/h. The thief will be caught at ________.
solution:
**Given:**

A thief steals a bike at 12:30 p.m. and drives it at 48 km/h.

The bike owner starts to chase him on another bike at 58 km/h.

**Concept used:**

Time taken to meet = Initial Distance / Relative

Speed Distance = speed × time

**Calculation:**

In 30 min the thief will cover 48 × 1/2

⇒ 24 km

Now,

The owner need to cover up this 24 km to catch the thief

Relative speed = 58 - 48

⇒ 10 km/h

Time = 24/10

⇒ 2.4 hour or 2 hours 24 minutes [As 1 hour = 60 minutes]

So, the thief will be caught at 1 p.m + 2 hour and 24 minutes

⇒ 3:24 p.m

**∴ The thief will be caught at 3:24 p.m.**
